review_level: Source triage of summaries, function/option names and lexical command references; not a line-by-line behavioral or acceptance review.

batches.title: Boot, snapshots and installed-system recovery
batches.language: Shell; isolate privileged target operations from per-user UI.
batches.scope: Fresh opt-in Limine installation/refresh, matched-kernel read-only overlay previews and confirmed offline restore with retained roots/boot files and durable interruption recovery exist in QEMU. Next: automatic Snapper menu synchronization and bounded capacity. Encryption, hibernation, direct UKI boot and factory reset need separate fixtures.
batches.acceptance: Fresh UEFI disk boot with ISO detached; real kernel and bootloader upgrades; preserved custom settings; snapshot boot with matching kernel/modules; explicit restore and failed-boot recovery. No host disk or bootloader changes.

batches.title: Packages, channels, upgrades and migrations
batches.language: Shell. Keep versioned migrations and compatible public command paths.
batches.scope: Local read-only readiness/status and private atomic update-stage records exist; failures stop later required stages and worker-held locks/interruption/retry are VM-tested. Next: detached transactions, keyring/channel validation, restart advice and failure recovery. Review cache/orphan/AUR/mise handling independently; the Omarchy quattro migration is source-specific and needs Titan lifecycle design rather than literal reproduction.
batches.acceptance: VM full upgrades, lock contention, low space, interrupted transactions, preserved user choices and recoverable errors; no implicit reboot, forced conflict overwrite or unrequested removal.

batches.title: Agent launch, accounts, usage and optional runtimes
batches.language: Shell orchestration and QML views; provider protocols require a documented implementation decision.
batches.scope: Current agent selection/launch/skills are a base. Separate account registry, authenticated provider usage, process environments, provider installers and gateways. Never inherit upstream permission-bypass switches or copy credentials into logs.
batches.acceptance: Isolated fake profiles plus explicit real-login checks where authorized; launch arguments stay exact; concurrent account state and stale/offline usage handling; removal preserves user data unless separately requested.

batches.title: Theme lifecycle, palettes, applications and branding
batches.language: Shell for lifecycle/rendering orchestration; QML for chooser, previews and reactive consumers.
batches.scope: Finish import/install/update/remove, validated palette/template schema and application reloads; preserve the graphite baseline. Separate cross-machine sync and hardware RGB adapters. Omarchy templates and fonts cannot be used as Titan runtime dependencies.
batches.acceptance: Import a new theme, reject invalid or linked files, update and remove safely, restore original preferences, and inspect real app rendering/reload. Font switching and screenshots at matched scale.

batches.title: Authentication, privilege and SSH service lifecycle
batches.language: Shell with reviewed privileged templates and root validation.
batches.scope: Add SSH agent/server lifecycle, FIDO2/fingerprint PAM setup/removal and command-scoped privilege contracts. Passwordless sudo and Docker-group access change security boundaries; expose explicit choices rather than enabling them through a broad port.
batches.acceptance: Disposable VM PAM/sudo validation and refusal paths before hardware tests; preserve a recovery login; track owned firewall rules and authorized keys; no secret or key output.

batches.title: Detection, monitors, input, audio tuning and power
batches.language: Shell for detected system operations; QML/native services for reactive state; Lua compositor rules.
batches.scope: Extend conservative hardware profiles and safe display recovery, DDC/Apple brightness, input and audio adapters. Distinguish read-only predicates from driver/sysfs mutations. Portable power policy must not alter the owner's always-awake policy.
batches.acceptance: VM monitor fixtures plus explicitly documented physical-device tests; unplug recovery, no available internal-output lockout, profile matching, audio/output checks and reduced-motion paths.

batches.title: Optional service lifecycle and file sharing
batches.language: Shell operations; QML status and controls using native events when available.
batches.scope: Extend existing Docker/CUPS/Tailscale lifecycle, receipt/send and owned activation units. Third-party services need separate setup/auth/remove recipes; DNS changes must preserve working connections and pre-existing configuration.
batches.acceptance: Real package setup/start/disable/re-enable and restore; no socket reactivation after disable; explicit external authentication/device tests; owned firewall and data preservation.

batches.title: Developer environments, config recovery and workspace jobs
batches.language: Shell for system tools, mise, jobs and per-user config operations.
batches.scope: Developer environment recipes and local Compose database lifecycles now use original Bash; Node/Laravel and all five edited-config/data-persistence paths pass focused QEMU acceptance. Next: remaining developer jobs (SSH-forward/rsync/tmux/worktrees), defaults/launchers and configuration recovery with real fixtures. Preserve user data, locks, backups and compatible paths.
batches.acceptance: Real provisioning, executable tools and Bash activation; worktree and backup data preservation; authenticated localhost SSH forward and rsync event delivery; unit/process cleanup; no implicit mise project trust.

batches.title: Application bundles, browser integration, gaming and launchers
batches.language: Shell, declarative catalogs and desktop files; QML selectors.
batches.scope: Separate package availability from complete provisioning. Add paired install/remove behavior, native messaging/protocol handlers, TUI and retro launchers, GPU-aware gaming and a dedicated Windows VM milestone. Removal defaults preserve profiles, models, saves and game libraries.
batches.acceptance: Actual official/AUR package builds in guests; quoted filenames/URLs; default launch/cwd behavior; native messaging framing and protocol ownership; install/remove restores previous user choices.

batches.title: Plugin manifest, catalog, cloning and updates
batches.language: QML extensions and Shell lifecycle management; maintain Titan's own manifest/API.
batches.scope: Extend existing install/validate/enable/disable/remove with built-in clone, catalog, capability reporting and validated update rollback. A renamed Omarchy plugin is not compatible with Titan automatically.
batches.acceptance: Real QML load/unload; broken update restores a working plugin; enabled registry and user edits remain intact; permissions and compatibility are reviewable.

batches.title: Capture, media, dictation and picker workflows
batches.language: Shell tool orchestration and QML interactive controls.
batches.scope: Finish frozen screenshot selection, webcam synchronization, safe file/timezone picking, ASCII conversion and explicit Voxtype model provisioning/status. Preserve clipboard and QR secrecy.
batches.acceptance: Real files and frames, output preservation, cancellation/keyboard navigation, recording teardown and dictated input on explicitly tested hardware; no private-content logs.

batches.title: Shell surfaces, notifications, toggles, state and watchers
batches.language: QML/native Quickshell APIs for UI/reactive services; Shell CLI adapters.
batches.scope: Replace generic state/file-flag helpers with documented Titan preferences and operations. Add persistent reminders, battery/crash watchers, weather state and shell restart/reload contracts. Preserve researched appearance and exact key chords.
batches.acceptance: Actual Wayland/QML interactions, event lifetimes and CPU cost, persistence/restart and reduced motion; restore panel/theme baseline; no broad application killing.

batches.title: Shared command primitives and distribution diagnostics
batches.language: Shell shared helpers; development analysis/tests may use Python.
batches.scope: Implement stable command-presence, diagnostics and selection contracts where needed. Drive selection/password and log upload require narrowly scoped UI/privileged workflows; never expose firmware keys or auto-upload logs.
batches.acceptance: Argument boundaries, missing-command exit codes and side-effect-free status; cancel leaves state unchanged; explicit redacted-log upload destination before network writes.
